Handbook/News types/Body:
Here you can add, edit or delete news types.



News types are used to categorize news published on the homepage.
Handbook/Shifts/Body:
Here you can add, edit or delete shifts.



Shifts are used alongside teams to show who is working, has worked, and will work. This can facilitate and enable trend analyses, follow-ups, etc.

Explanations

Cycle length (weeks) - Used to specify the length of a schedule cycle. If the work schedule always looks the same, this can be left at 1 week.



Reference week - Only filled in when a new shift is created and cannot be edited afterwards. This is used so that week 1 has a reference point.



Teams - Select which teams will work in this schedule. For example: If you create a 3-shift schedule, you should select 3 teams.
Handbook/Shift teams/Body:
Here you can add, edit or delete teams.



Teams are used alongside shifts to show who is working, has worked, and will work. This can facilitate and enable trend analyses, follow-ups, etc.



A team can be used in multiple shifts. Example: If you have a team named "Shift 1" you can use it in your 3-shift and 5-shift.
Handbook/Unit groups/Body:
Here you can add, edit or delete unit groups.



Unit groups are used to categorize units.
Handbook/Units/Body:
Here you can add, edit or delete units.



Units are used to represent individual entities within the system. Example: A business has a production line called "Filling". This line can then be created as a unit with the same name.

Explanations

Group - Select which group the unit belongs to.



Plannable - Whether the unit can be used for planning or not. If disabled, the unit will only be usable for reporting.



Columns - These are used to report data in the reporting view. Example: If it is desired that a unit can report the hourly production output, a column needs to be added for this.



Categories - If the unit reports an event, categories can be used to specify what type of event it is.



Shifts - Select which shift types the unit can be staffed by.
Handbook/Categories/Body:
Here you can add, edit or delete categories.



Categories are used to specify types of events on a unit.

Explanations

Sub categories - Here you can create sub categories for a category. Example: If you have a category called "Machine failure" you can create sub categories like "Electrical failure", "Mechanical failure", etc.
Handbook/Unit columns/Body:
Here you can add, edit or delete unit columns.



Unit columns are used to report specific data related to each unit. Example: If you want to track the hourly production output of a unit, you would add a column for this purpose.

Explanations

Data type - What type of data the column will hold, such as number or text.



(Number only) Compare to previous hour - If enabled, the reported value will be compared to the value from the previous hour to show trends.



(Text only) Large column - If enabled, the column will be displayed larger in the reporting view for easier data entry.
Handbook/Master plans/Body:
Here you can add, edit or delete master plans.



Master plans are used to plan activities within a unit.

Explanations

Fields - Here you can specify which fields can be filled in. Example: Planned start date, Material number, and Material description.



Allow removing elements - If enabled, elements in the master plan can be removed after they have been created. Note that an element can always be striked through.



Allow import from Excel - If enabled, .xlsx files can be imported into the master plan according to set import rules.
Handbook/Master plan fields/Body:
Here you can add, edit or delete master plan fields.



Master plan fields are used to describe activities in the master plan.

Explanations

Data type - What type of data the column will hold, such as number, text, or date.



Alignment - Whether the content in each cell should be left-aligned, centered, or right-aligned.
Handbook/Import rules/Body:
If you wish to import Excel files for master plans, you need to map fields here.



Note the following:

  • You can only set import rules on master plans that allow import from Excel
  • Fields that arent mapped will not be imported
Explanations

Replace master plan on import - If this option is enabled, all elements in the master plan will be replaced during import.



Skip row 1 on import - If this option is enabled, row 1 in the Excel file will be skipped on import.



Select column from Excel... - Here you map fields to columns in Excel. Example: The field Planned start date should get its data from the column BC in the Excel file.



Group key - If your Excel file contains a column that groups elements together, you can select it here. Example: If you have a column named Group ID in your Excel file, and elements with the same Group ID should belong to the same group in the master plan, you can select this column as the group key.
Handbook/Users/Body:
Here you can add, edit or delete users.

Explanations

Administrator - An administrator can manage most of the system except user data.



Developer - A developer can manage everything in the system.



Reporter - A reporter can report in the system.



Planner - A planner can view planning in the system.



Master Planner - A master planner can view and manage planning in the system.
Handbook/Audit trail/Body: All events that change data in the system are logged here. You can only see information based on your permissions.
Handbook/Home/Body:
Here you can log in and see news. Users who are logged in can create trend panels to customize the tracking of data in the system.



Administrators can create, edit, or delete news on the home page.
Handbook/Unit/Body:
All users can view reporting for a unit, but the Reporter permission is required to actually report.



To report data in a column, click the Report data button at the top left or click the pencil in the cell you want to report in.



To report an event, such as a disruption, click the Report events button at the top left or click the row you want to report in and then the plus sign.



To change the staffing type, click the Change staffing type button at the top right.
Handbook/Master plan/Body:
All users can view master planning, but the Master Planner permission is required to make changes to the master plan.



To make changes, the plan must first be checked out. Note that if you force a checkout, the person who had checked out the plan will lose their changes.



Once you have checked out the plan, you can:

  • Choose whether you want to affect a single element (Element mode) or all elements in the selected element's group (Group mode)
  • Add new elements
  • Duplicate the selected element
  • Edit fields in elements
  • Move elements up and down. Activate Standalone element if you want the selected element not to be able to connect to existing groups
  • Strike through elements
  • Delete elements (if this is allowed for the master plan)
  • Import master plan to import from an Excel document. Note that you need to set up import rules first

Changing the master plan is not recommended in mobile mode.
